chunks: (44) Muhammad bin Hammam said: Ja'far bin Muhammad bin Malik narrated to me, saying: Umar bin Tarkhan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad bin Isma'il narrated to me, from Ali bin Umar bin Ali bin al-Husayn, from Abu Abdullah Ja'far bin Muhammad, that he said:

The Qa'im is from my offspring; he will live the lifespan of the Khalil (Abraham), one hundred and twenty years, and he will be known. Then he will undergo a long occultation, and then he will appear in the form of a successful young man of thirty-two years old, until a group of people turn away from him. He will fill the earth with equity and justice, just as it was filled with tyranny and oppression.

key_terms.الْخَلِيلُ: The Friend, referring to Prophet Abraham
key_terms.الْغَيْبَةُ: The Occultation, the period of concealment
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser/Exister, a title for the Twelfth Imam

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics and lifespan of the Qa'im according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the longevity of Al-Qa'im, comparing his lifespan to Abraham's (200 years), which underscores the divine preservation of the Imam during his extended occultation. It emphasizes his reappearance at age thirty-two to establish universal justice, a theme resonating with the Shia eschatological expectation of the Mahdi filling the earth with equity as it was filled with tyranny.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (44) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from Umar bin Tarkhan from Muhammad bin Issma’eel from Ali bin Umar bin Ali bin al-Husayn (as) that Abu Abdullah Ja’far bin Muhammad as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“Al-Qa’im is one of my descendants. His old is like Abraham’s old; one hundred and twenty years. He is recognized and then he disappears for a period of time and then he reappears as a young man of thirty-two years old. Some groups of people deviate from him. He fills the world with justice after it has been filled with injustice and oppression.”
